A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CORE: Collaborative Reasoning via Cross Teaching. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, training curves, and qualitative evaluations in Sections 5–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds non-oracle selection, sensitivity, three-model scaling, and cross-dataset transfer results.

M1.justification: Equation (5) changes the optional trace-accuracy bonus from correctness multiplied by rho to correctness multiplied by 1−rho_r, favoring successful traces on instances where fewer traces succeed. This revises one reward component; the two-round cross-teaching procedure, DPP-lite, and rescue mechanism remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: GSM8K, MATH, AIME, and GPQA remain the evaluated benchmarks. Appendix H adds cross-dataset generalization scenarios: AIME-trained models are evaluated on MATH and GSM8K without target-dataset fine-tuning.

E2.justification: The new AIME comparison evaluates majority-vote and agreement-gated selection alongside best-single-model and oracle selection (v2 Table 3). Existing Base, SD-E2, oracle-pair, and larger-single-model comparisons retain their membership. MALT and MAPoRL are described in Table 6 but are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds non-oracle selection protocols, three-model evaluation including an 8B collaborator, parameter/distance sweeps, and transfer without further fine-tuning. Appendix D reports 4096-token AIME baseline reevaluation, although v1 already states that global cap. Appendix I reports 770 training examples, conflicting with 792 in both abstracts; an actual split change is unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 adds reward/hint-parameter sensitivity, hybrid-versus-cosine distance testing, two-versus-three-model scaling, cross-dataset transfer, and practical-versus-oracle selection analyses (Tables 3 and 7–10). These substantially broaden the questions tested about robustness, generalization, and deployment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new sensitivity ranges describe variation across parameter settings, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and the original ablation scores are unchanged. v1 Table 4 becomes v2 Table 5, replacing AIME SD-E2 Pass@1 values: Qwen2.5-7B 16.40→26.00, Phi-3-small-8k 12.00→20.00, and Ministral-3-8B 18.50→51.50 under reported reevaluation. New results include three-model AIME oracle/majority/agreement scores of 82.60/81.20/80.40 and AIME-trained transfer Pass@1 of 75.90 on MATH and 86.35 on GSM8K.

T1.justification: The auxiliary-reward definition in Equation (5) changes mathematically through the replacement of rho by 1−rho_r. The collaboration-gain theorem, DPP-lite separation proposition, and their proofs remain substantively unchanged. The newly displayed inclusion–exclusion identity and reformatted complexity expression restate existing reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract adds the claim that three-model majority voting closes most of the oracle-selection gap and explicitly labels the retained headline results as oracle Team Pass@2. The central contributions concerning training-time cross-teaching, complementary correctness, and low-data learning remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds a hard-instance curriculum interpretation of the revised auxiliary reward and interpretations of the new sensitivity, scaling, transfer, and selection results. Appendix I introduces a specific AIME contamination caveat with estimated model cutoffs. The original error analysis, deployment discussion, and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents AIME year coverage, parameter-sweep values, the three-model composition, and selector rules. Existing prompts, LoRA settings, and runtime information largely remain unchanged. The explicit code-repository link on v1's first page is removed without replacement; this establishes reduced access information, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix E add MALT and MAPoRL, distinguishing CORE's instance-conditioned peer teaching from role-specialized pipelines and discussion-based multi-agent RL. The remaining positioning is largely retained; SD-E2 consolidation and GPQA publication updates concern existing cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, reward explanation, and related-work passages receive targeted revisions, with terminology, author-name, and header corrections. A non-oracle subsection and Appendices E–I are inserted; the original ablations and discussion become J–K. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial tabular presentation for selection, sensitivity, distance choice, scaling, transfer, related-method positioning, and contamination considerations (Tables 3 and 6–11). Existing tables and figures are redistributed and table captions move above tables. Figures 5–8 lose their clipped title bands while retaining the same plotted curves.

improvement.justification: The sensitivity and transfer tests, clearer oracle labeling, and closer related-work discussion improve the paper's evidence and interpretability. However, Section 5.2 describes apparently equivalent selectors while Table 3 reports different scores, Appendix I's 770 training examples conflict with the abstract's 792, and the code link is removed. These reporting problems limit the practical-selection claim and reproducibility, making the net improvement limited.
